newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Di Tella says U.S. "carnal relations" over.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Di Tella says U.S. "carnal relations" over.

text.p: Argentina's "carnal relations" with the United States are over now that the country is firmly part of the Western alliance, Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella said in an interview on Saturday.

In the early 1990s, Di Tella caused controversy in Argentina, long a nonaligned nation with a history of anti- Americanism, when he described the new, friendlier relations with the United States as "carnal."
But he told the La Nacion newspaper that Argentine relations with the United States were now on solid enough ground to allow for a more critical, less passionate, posture.
"At the beginning we needed to clearly and categorically affirm our alignment with the West, but that stage has now passed. Now we can criticise American commercial policies," Di Tella said.
"After all these years, some things are now taken for granted," he added, describing "carnal relations" as "part of the first period."

South America's Mercosur trade bloc -- which includes the continent's two giants, Argentina and Brazil -- are locked in tough negotiations with the United States over the creation of a free-trade area throughout the Americas.
Talks two weeks ago in the Brazilian city of Belo Horizonte failed to make much progress, and the South Americans are also considering a rival free-trade offer from the European Union.
Argentina ended decades of economic isolationism and non alignment when current Peronist President Carlos Menem came to power in 1989, privatising industries and inviting foreign investment.
